proof_summary: Euler’s criterion and a binomial expansion factor the reduction modulo $p$ into Vandermonde and diagonal factors, while the half-Wilson identity $C^2=(-1)^{(p+1)/2}$ makes the remaining scalar nonzero when $p\equiv1\pmod4$ and also proves nonsingularity of the auxiliary matrix with coefficient $-C$ when $p\equiv3\pmod4$. In the latter case $C=\pm1$, and a quadratic-character sum yields $AB^T+BA^T=0$ for the target matrix $A$ and that auxiliary matrix $B$; since the dimension is odd and $B$ is nonsingular, taking determinants forces $\det A=0$.
